content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Research on coupling hydrological models with Sentinel-1 SAR observations can constrain satellite-derived soil saturation estimates in drained agricultural plains, reducing misclassification in fields with shallow moisture variations.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-05104","field":"abstract","quote":"Simulated soil saturation deficit was used as a prior to constrain per-scene SAR thresholds"}]},{"text":"Water-cloud model inversion of SAR backscatter is sensitive to soil moisture in the range relevant to field agriculture, with retrieval errors increasing substantially when soil volumetric water content exceeds 0.35 m³/m³.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-05101","field":"abstract","quote":"errors increased by 30–40 % when soil volumetric water content exceeded 0.35 m³/m³"}]},{"text":"Dual-polarisation SAR classification can distinguish vegetation water content and surface conditions that confound single-polarisation backscatter, potentially supporting more robust soil moisture discrimination in mixed crop-soil landscapes.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-05103","field":"abstract","quote":"The VH/VV ratio proved the most important feature for separating flooded"}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher has demonstrated methods to invert SAR backscatter for hydrological variables and acknowledge soil moisture confounding in agricultural settings [SYN-PUB-05101, SYN-PUB-05104], but the published work focuses on flood and inundation mapping rather than continuous field-scale soil moisture estimation for yield prediction or health mapping."}
